name: Yanji–KCC planned technical-workforce intake (2014 historical context)

attribution.legal_posture: The 2014 source describes the reported activity at a general level; illegality, deception, sanctions-evasion, and enforcement status require separate evidence.

organizations: KCC (as written in the 2014 Yanji report)
caveats: Treat 1,600 and 2,000 as separate plans or targets; they represent planned figures rather than completed headcounts or a combined total.

KCC remains an exact organization reference to existing historical coverage; create no new person or front-company profile. Planned intake completion and fraudulent employment by every worker require separate evidence.
An unspecified KCC transliteration or organizational component remains distinct from later KCC-linked entities unless an exact source link connects them.
Personnel labels remain source-specific; fraudulent remote-worker classification requires case-level evidence.

This is an aggregate record; named person, facilitator, persona, account, prosecution, front-company, sensitive-identifier, address, payment-selector, identity-document, and image profiles require separate source records.
The acronym KCC is retained exactly as written. It remains separate from every Korea Computer Center alias, component, or later company record unless a source links them.
The source establishes a planned intake; completion of either target remains a separate outcome.
This is historical workforce and organizational context; fraudulent employment, deception, sanctions evasion, misconduct, and current-operation status remain unestablished.

statements: Yanji High-Tech Zone reported that it had signed an agreement with a DPRK organization identified only as KCC and planned to introduce 1,600 technical personnel.
The same report's 2014 work plan separately targeted bringing 2,000 DPRK IT and technology personnel into the science and technology innovation park.
The two figures are separate plans or targets; the source does not establish completed intake and they must not be added together as a realized workforce count.
Original-language evidence: “目前已与朝鲜KCC签订协议，拟引进1600名技术人员，并提供稳定的居住、用工政策环境。” The same report's 2014 plan stated: “科技创新园项目完成投资2.2亿元……引进朝鲜IT科技人才2000名”。

Researcher-supplied English translation: The report said Yanji High-Tech Zone had signed an agreement with North Korea's KCC and planned to introduce 1,600 technical personnel while providing stable residence and employment-policy conditions. Its 2014 work plan separately targeted bringing 2,000 DPRK IT and technology personnel into the science and technology innovation park.
infrastructure.translation_method: Close researcher translation of the reviewed Simplified Chinese official text; KCC retained exactly as written.
limitations: Describe 1,600 and 2,000 as separate plans or targets, not completed headcounts and not a combined total.
Do not retroactively label all personnel as fraudulent remote workers.
Do not infer that an unspecified KCC transliteration or organizational component is identical to every later KCC-linked entity without exact source linkage.
The acronym KCC is retained exactly as written. It is not expanded or merged into every Korea Computer Center alias, component, or later company record.
The source establishes a planned intake, not completion of either target.
This is historical workforce and organizational context, not proof of fraudulent employment, deception, sanctions evasion, misconduct, or a current operation.
No named person, facilitator, persona, account, prosecution, front company, sensitive identifier, address, payment selector, identity document, or image is retained.
